question_text: In quadrilateral ABCD, the diagonal [BD] has length 8 km. Find the length of the diagonal [AC].

subparts.stem: In quadrilateral ABCD, the diagonal [BD] has length 8 km. Find the length of the diagonal [AC].

mark_breakdown.desc: Use cosine rule to find angle $\theta$ in $\triangle\text{ABD}$
Use cosine rule to find angle $\phi$ in $\triangle\text{DBC}$
Apply cosine rule in $\triangle\text{ABC}$ to find $\text{AC}$

subparts.solution:
By the cosine rule in $\triangle\text{ABD}$:
$$\cos \theta = \frac{8^2 + 4^2 - 5^2}{2 \times 8 \times 4}$$
$$\cos \theta = \frac{55}{64}$$
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{55}{64}\right) \approx 30.8^\circ$$

By the cosine rule in $\triangle\text{DBC}$:
$$\cos \phi = \frac{8^2 + 6^2 - 6^2}{2 \times 8 \times 6}$$
$$\cos \phi = \frac{64}{96} = \frac{2}{3}$$
$$\phi = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 48.2^\circ$$

Now $\text{A}\hat{\text{B}}\text{C} = \theta + \phi \approx 30.8^\circ + 48.2^\circ \approx 78.9^\circ$

By the cosine rule in $\triangle\text{ABC}$:
$$\text{AC}^2 \approx 4^2 + 6^2 - 2 \times 4 \times 6 \times \cos 78.9^\circ$$
$$\text{AC} \approx \sqrt{4^2 + 6^2 - 2 \times 4 \times 6 \times \cos 78.9^\circ}$$
$$\text{AC} \approx 6.54\text{ km}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The cosine rule for an angle is $\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}$, and for a side is $a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A$.
step_by_step: Find angle $\theta$ at vertex $B$ in triangle $ABD$ using the side lengths $8, 4, 5$.
Find angle $\phi$ at vertex $B$ in triangle $DBC$ using the side lengths $8, 6, 6$.
Sum angles $\theta$ and $\phi$ to obtain the total angle $\text{A}\hat{\text{B}}\text{C} \approx 78.9^\circ$.
Use the cosine rule in the outer triangle $ABC$ with sides $AB = 4$, $BC = 6$, and angle $78.9^\circ$ to find $AC$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding intermediate angles too early, which can lead to slight inaccuracies in the final answer.
